Residual degrees of freedom of the first stage

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_residual_df.Rd

Returns \(\nu_e\), the residual degrees of freedom that the Fisher factor of the conditional-association test uses in the form \(\nu_e-|S|-2\), when the first stage fixes it exactly, and says why it does not otherwise.

Usage

mc_residual_df(fit)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_residual_df'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

fit

an object of class "mcglm_graph" or "mcglm".

x

an object of class "mcg_residual_df".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_residual_df": a list with df, the value of \(\nu_e\) or NA; exact, a logical; n, the number of observations; rank, the common rank \(h\) of the designs or NA; and why, a character vector with the reasons the correction is not exact, empty when it is. The print method returns x invisibly.

When the correction is exact

The Pearson residuals of a Gaussian response with identity link and constant variance are the least-squares residuals of its design, scaled. When every response has that form and the same column space of design, of rank \(h\), the residual covariance is the sample covariance after projecting out a common \(h\)-dimensional space. For Gaussian responses its partial correlations are then distributed as those of a sample covariance with \(n-h\) degrees of freedom, that of \(n-h+1\) observations with an estimated mean, so \(\nu_e=n-h\). With the intercept alone, \(h=1\) and \(\nu_e-|S|-2=n-|S|-3\), the factor used when no correction is supplied. Outside that case no finite-sample correction is established and none is offered: the function returns exact = FALSE with the reasons, and the approximation by \(n\) (df_residual = NULL in the separation routines) is the one to use. The check requires constant variance, the identity link, an identity within-response structure, unit first-stage weights, and designs of equal rank spanning the same column space for all responses.

See also

mc_pc_skeleton, whose df_residual accepts it, and mc_graph_pipeline, where df_residual = "auto" calls it.

Other structure discovery: mc_find_vstructures(), mc_ges(), mc_graph_pipeline(), mc_orient_meek(), mc_pc_skeleton(), mc_separating_sets(), mc_skeleton_to_bnlearn()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1); n <- 60; x <- rnorm(n); g <- gl(3, 20)
d <- data.frame(y1 = rnorm(n), y2 = rnorm(n), y3 = rnorm(n), x = x, g = g)
f <- mcglm_graph(list(y1 ~ x + g, y2 ~ x + g, y3 ~ x + g), data = d)
#> Automatic initial values selected.
mc_residual_df(f)          # 60 - 4
#> Residual degrees of freedom: 56 (n = 60, rank of the design = 4)
# }
